name: Sugar Push
summary: The foundational pattern of modern swing: a compress-and-release conversation danced in place in the slot.
steps: Counts 1–2: the follower walks forward down the slot while the lead settles back to make space.
Counts 3&4: triple step into gentle compression. Hands meet at waist height, weight eases forward.
Release the compression like a spring; the follower travels back the way they came.
Counts 5&6: both anchor with a triple step at your own end of the slot, keeping stretch through the arm.

countRows.t: Anchor triple at the end of the slot

mistakes.w: Pulling with the arms instead of moving from your center.
mistakes.f: Keep elbows soft and heavy. The connection starts at your feet, not your biceps.

mistakes.w: Skipping the anchor and drifting straight into the next move.
mistakes.f: Finish 5&6 completely. The anchor is where the stretch (and the fun) lives.

name: Left Side Pass
summary: The follower travels past the lead’s left side and the two swap ends of the slot. Your bread-and-butter traveling pattern.
steps: Counts 1–2: the lead steps back and slightly left, opening the slot and inviting the follower forward.
Counts 3&4: the follower passes down the lead’s left side with a triple step; the lead redirects gently with the left hand at chest height.
Both turn to face each other as the follower reaches the far end.
Counts 5&6: anchor triple. Ends swapped, connection stretched, ready for the next pattern.

countRows.t: Walk, walk: follower enters the slot
Passing triple down the left side

mistakes.w: The lead stands in the slot and forces the follower around them.
mistakes.f: Clear sideways out of the lane. The slot belongs to the follower.

mistakes.w: Steering the follower with a big arm swing.
mistakes.f: Lead with your body moving out of the way; the hand just describes the lane.

name: Underarm Pass
summary: A right-side pass where the follower travels under the lead’s raised arm. The gateway to every turning pattern.
steps: Counts 1–2: the lead raises the joined hand to about eye level, inviting the follower forward.
Counts 3&4: the follower passes on the lead’s right side, traveling under the arm with a triple step.
The lead’s hand traces a soft halo: no cranking, no pushing the hand down.
Counts 5&6: anchor at opposite ends, lower the hands naturally into connection.

countRows.t: Walk, walk: hand rises to eye level

mistakes.w: Raising the arm late so the follower has to duck.
mistakes.f: The hand is up by the end of count 2. Think doorway, not limbo bar.

mistakes.w: Gripping the follower’s hand through the pass.
mistakes.f: Loose fingertips. The follower’s hand should be able to swivel freely.

name: Sugar Tuck
summary: A sugar push that ends in a turn: compress, tuck the follower slightly inward, then release into a free outward spin.
steps: Counts 1–2: enter exactly like a sugar push, follower forward, lead settles.
Counts 3&4: tuck. The lead rotates the follower slightly inward during compression, loading the spring.
Release: the rebound sends the follower into an outward underarm turn.
Counts 5&6: the follower finishes the rotation and both anchor.

countRows.t: Tuck: compress and rotate slightly in

mistakes.w: Cranking the turn with the arm like a steering wheel.
mistakes.f: The turn comes from the tuck’s rebound. Your hand is a pivot point, not a motor.

mistakes.w: The follower spins without finishing the tuck first.
mistakes.f: Wait for the compression. No spring, no spin.

name: Inside Turn
summary: A left side pass with a turn in the middle: the follower rotates toward the lead under the joined hand while traveling.
steps: Counts 1–2: set up like a left side pass, but raise the joined hand by count 2.
Counts 3&4: the follower turns left (toward the lead) under the arm while continuing down the slot.
Keep the halo small and directly over the follower’s head.
Counts 5&6: finish the rotation, settle into the anchor.

countRows.t: Traveling inside turn under the arm

mistakes.w: Turning on the spot and stalling in the middle of the slot.
mistakes.f: Keep traveling. The turn happens on the way down the slot, not instead of it.

mistakes.w: Lead’s thumb clamps down mid-turn.
mistakes.f: Flat, open hand. The follower borrows it; you don’t own it.

name: Free Spin
summary: The lead releases connection entirely and the follower spins solo down the slot. Trust, momentum, and a clean spot.
steps: Counts 1–2: set up like an underarm pass with slightly more momentum into the slot.
On 3, release the hand with a clear, small signal. No shove.
Counts 3&4: the follower spots the far end of the slot and spins through the triple.
Counts 5&6: re-collect the connection gently and anchor together.

mistakes.w: Over-leading the spin with a big windup.
mistakes.f: The follower generates the spin. Your job is a clean release and a clear lane.

mistakes.w: Drifting off the slot line mid-spin.
mistakes.f: Spot the end of the slot before you go. Eyes lead, body follows.

name: The Whip
summary: The signature 8-count of modern swing: the follower is caught at count 4 and redirected back down the slot with a smooth, elastic whip action.
steps: Counts 1–2: the follower enters the slot like a pass; the lead steps in beside the lane.
Counts 3–4: the lead catches with the right arm across the follower’s back and pivots, redirecting their momentum.
Counts 5–6: post and send. The follower travels back down the slot the way they came.
Counts 7&8: both anchor with stretch. That elastic finish is the whole point.

mistakes.w: Muscling the redirection with the right arm.
mistakes.f: The pivot of your whole body redirects the follower. The arm just keeps the connection.

mistakes.w: Letting the slot collapse into a circle.
mistakes.f: Think railroad track: the follower leaves and returns on the same line.

name: Whip w/ Outside Turn
summary: A whip where the follower adds an outside turn on the way back down the slot. The first big whip variation everyone learns.
steps: Counts 1–4: dance the first half of a standard whip: enter, catch, pivot.
On 5, the lead raises the joined hand instead of posting low.
Counts 5–6: the follower turns right (away from the lead) under the arm while traveling back down the slot.
Counts 7&8: finish the rotation and anchor with stretch.

mistakes.w: Raising the hand at 3 and telegraphing the turn too early.
mistakes.f: Keep the whip honest through 4. The turn is announced on 5, not before.

mistakes.w: The follower turns in place at the post.
mistakes.f: Travel first, turn along the way. The slot still ends where it always does.

name: Basket Whip
summary: A two-hand whip danced through a wrapped “sweetheart” position. Close, showy, and all about frame.
steps: Counts 1–2: from a two-hand connection, the lead draws the follower in and wraps them into sweetheart position, follower’s back to the lead’s chest.
Counts 3–4: travel together through the whip’s catch, keeping both hands connected in the wrap.
Counts 5–6: unwrap. The lead unwinds the follower back down the slot.
Counts 7&8: anchor at full stretch, two hands or one.

countRows.t: Draw in and wrap to sweetheart

mistakes.w: The wrap turns into a headlock.
mistakes.f: Hands stay at the follower’s waist height. The follower should be able to stand tall the whole time.

mistakes.w: Rushing the unwrap and losing the follower’s balance.
mistakes.f: Unwind on 5–6, not 4&. Give the rotation its full two counts.

name: Barrel Roll
summary: A rolling traveling turn where the follower passes through a wrapped position and unrolls down the slot in one continuous motion.
steps: Counts 1–2: enter with two hands and begin rotating the follower into a wrap, like the start of a basket.
Counts 3–4: instead of holding the wrap, keep the rotation rolling. The follower turns continuously through it.
Counts 5–6: the roll unwinds and carries the follower down the slot.
Counts 7&8: catch the connection and anchor.

mistakes.w: Chopping the roll into separate turns.
mistakes.f: It’s one continuous rotation. Think rolling a barrel, not flipping pages.

mistakes.w: Losing the slot during the roll.
mistakes.f: The roll travels. Keep the follower’s path pointed at the end of the lane.

name: The Lean
summary: A simple supported lean for phrase endings: the follower tips a few degrees off axis while keeping their own weight.
steps: Signal early: a clear compression and a stilled frame tell the follower a lean is coming. Never surprise a dip.
On 1, the follower shifts slightly off axis in one straight line, head to heel.
The lead supports with frame: forearm and posture, not biceps.
Hold for a beat, then recover on the next count 1 together.

countRows.t: Settle into the lean: one straight line

mistakes.w: The follower gives the lead all their weight.
mistakes.f: Keep your core on. A lean is borrowed balance, not a trust fall.

mistakes.w: No exit plan: the music ends and nobody knows how to get up.
mistakes.f: Agree on the recovery before you need it: recover on the next downbeat, together.

name: Sweetheart Dip
summary: A dramatic dip from the wrapped sweetheart position. The big phrase-ending picture move, done safely.
steps: Counts 1–4: wrap into sweetheart position exactly like a basket whip entry.
Counts 5–6: the lead steps into a braced stance (one leg back, frame locked) and signals down.
The follower keeps one straight line and controls their own descent along the lead’s supporting arm.
Counts 7–8: recover together on the downbeat. Smile like you planned it.

mistakes.w: Dipping a follower who didn’t know it was coming.
mistakes.f: Dips are invitations, not commands. Clear signal, and only with partners who know the move.

mistakes.w: The lead bends at the waist and loses the base.
mistakes.f: Bend your knees, not your back. Your stance is the furniture the dip rests on.

name: The Pop
summary: A small hip-assisted air step: the follower pops a few inches off the floor. Workshop-only, never on the social floor.
steps: Learn this one in a workshop with mats and a spotter, not from this page alone.
Counts 1–4: whip entry with compression at the catch, both partners counting out loud at first.
On 5, the follower jumps as the lead assists from the hip. The lift comes from the jump, not the arms.
Counts 6–8: land toes-first into a soft anchor, connection re-established.

mistakes.w: Trying it during a social dance.
mistakes.f: House rule: aerials live in workshops with mats and spotters, never on the open floor.

mistakes.w: The lead lifts with arms and shoulders.
mistakes.f: The follower jumps; the lead redirects. If your arms are tired, you’re doing it wrong.
